reason: The proof is correct. Sylow theory gives unique normal Sylow 7-subgroups; the Sylow 3-subgroups provide complements and unique normal forms. Nonabelianness forces the conjugation exponent to be one of the two nontrivial cube roots 2 or 4 modulo 7, and replacing a generator of the order-3 subgroup by its inverse matches these actions. The resulting normal-form bijection respects the correctly derived multiplication law, hence is an isomorphism.
